# `sesam config print` renders the whole config as one document, with every
# include flattened into it - YAML by default, JSON with --json.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient age1tdy2pxsfwpxxe0c9cuwty8zpsv6uuhf4zyug5f9lfl982lh3tctqrw2ll7 --group dev

# A secret in a sub-config, included from the main file.
mkdir svc
cp token.env svc/token.env
exec sesam add --nested --group dev svc/token.env
exists svc/sesam.yml
exec sesam config print
stdout '^users:'
stdout '^  - name: bob'
stdout '^groups:'
stdout '^secrets:'
stdout '  - path: svc/token.env'
! stdout 'include'

exec sesam config print --json
stdout '"users": \['
stdout '"path": "svc/token.env"'
! stdout 'include'

# The output is itself a complete sesam.yml: used in place of the tree, it
# declares exactly what the audit log records.
exec sesam config print
cp stdout merged.yml
rm svc/sesam.yml
cp merged.yml sesam.yml
exec sesam config diff
! stdout .

-- token.env --
TOKEN=hunter2
